claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has been reported in a hierarchical-heterostructured state featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
High-resolution microscopy can quantitatively characterize multilevel chemical fluctuations and mesoscale features in HfNbTiVAl10.
Quantitative imaging descriptors can be used as inputs to a calibrated, physics-constrained machine-learning model.
A modest number of experimental samples is sufficient to train the proposed model.
Multilevel chemical fluctuations mediate the relationship between processing, microstructure, and macroscopic mechanical performance.
Mesoscale grain and connectivity metrics mediate the relationship between processing, microstructure, and macroscopic mechanical performance.
Reducing atomistic or multiphysics simulations to key microstructural descriptors captures the essential structure-property relationships.
Embedding known physical constraints in the surrogate model improves prediction efficiency relative to traditional methods.
The proposed model will predict Young's modulus within approximately 10% of experiment.
The proposed model will predict yield strength within approximately 10% of experiment.
The proposed model will predict fracture toughness within approximately 10% of experiment.
The proposed model will reduce computational cost by at least a factor of ten relative to full multiphysics or comprehensive simulation methods.
Prior thermophysical-parameter, CALPHAD, first-principles, and machine-learning approaches were computationally intensive or inefficient.
Prior approaches were less effective at predicting fracture properties such as toughness.
The model may become unreliable when the hierarchical microstructure deviates markedly from its training domain, including through coarsening or unexpected phase segregation.
The model may become unreliable at temperatures or strain rates far outside the proposed testing domain.
Prediction errors exceeding 10% for any key property or a computational speedup below tenfold across at least three independent batches would falsify the hypothesis.
